title: Energy Transition Measures and Other Amendments Bill
what_it_is: Energy Transition Measures and Other Amendments Bill

sections.label: Climate change and net-zero commitment
sections.summary: Singapore commits to achieving net-zero by 2050 because climate change threatens health, livelihoods and security.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are disproportionately impacted by climate change, which threatens our health, our livelihoods and our security.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is why Singapore has committed to achieving net-zero by 2050.

sections.label: Low-carbon electricity imports
sections.summary: EMA granted Conditional Approvals to two projects importing 1.4 gigawatts from Indonesia, with plans for up to 5.6 gigawatts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Last week, I announced that the Energy Market Authority (EMA) has granted Conditional Approvals to two new projects to import 1.4 gigawatts of low-carbon electricity from Indonesia to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In total, we have announced plans to import up to 5.6 gigawatts of low-carbon electricity from Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are on track to meeting our ambition of six gigawatts of imported electricity, or around one-third of our energy supply by, 2035.

sections.label: S$5 billion energy transition injection
sections.summary: An initial injection of S$5 billion in FY2024 strengthens Singapore's position for multi-decade energy transition investments.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: With an initial injection of S$5 billion in FY2024, this puts us in a stronger position to make critical investments to secure our multi-decade energy transition.

sections.label: EMA access to energy infrastructure
sections.summary: The second proposal empowers EMA to direct owners and occupiers of critical energy infrastructure to allow licensees access.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our second proposal thus empowers EMA to direct owners and occupiers of critical energy infrastructure to allow licensees to access critical energy infrastructure and to enter into agreements with licensees for the same purpose.

sections.label: Amendments for infrastructure access
sections.summary: Clauses 8 and 34 amend the Electricity Act and Gas Act to empower EMA to direct access when parties fail to agree.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: However, there could be instances where both parties fail to reach a commercial agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Hence, clauses 8 and 34 of the Bill amend the Electricity Act and Gas Act, to empower EMA to direct owners or occupiers of critical energy infrastructure to allow licensees access to their infrastructure.

sections.label: Approval for repurposing assets
sections.summary: The third proposal introduces approval obligations for persons owning, managing or controlling key electricity and gas assets intending to repurpose them.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our third proposal, introduces approval obligations if persons owning, managing or controlling key electricity and gas assets intend to repurpose such assets.

sections.label: EMA cost recovery amendment
sections.summary: Clause 6(2) amends the EMA Act to let EMA recover costs for energy security, market development and decarbonisation initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: However, EMA is unable to legally recover the operating costs of such a critical facility despite the security, the benefits it has conferred to all electricity users.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Therefore, clause 6(2) of the Bill amends the EMA Act to allow EMA to recover costs associated with energy security, market development and decarbonisation-related initiatives, while ensuring the proper functioning of our energy system.

sections.label: Central gas entity Gasco
sections.summary: A central gas entity, Gasco, will centralise gas procurement and supply to the power sector for economies of scale and more diverse sources.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: These entities' diversified gas portfolios mitigated the risks associated with market volatilities and helped Japan and Korea avoid severe gas disruptions during the energy crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is why we announced, in 2023, that we would establish a central gas entity, or Gasco for short, to centralise the procurement and supply of gas to the power sector.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This Gasco will create greater economies of scale, which will allow us to negotiate more favourable gas contracting terms, enter into longer-term gas contracts for more stable prices and supply and allow us to procure gas from more diverse sources.

sections.label: EMA power rationing power
sections.summary: Clause 17 amends the Electricity Act to empower EMA to implement power rationing with the Minister of Trade and Industry's approval.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Clause 17 of the Bill amends the Electricity Act to empower EMA to implement power rationing, with the approval of the Minister of Trade and Industry.

sections.label: Liability protection for rationing compliance
sections.summary: Clause 17 amends the Electricity Act to protect businesses from liability if complying with EMA's power rationing direction breaches contracted obligations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Clause 17 of the Bill amends the Electricity Act to provide businesses with protection from liability if compliance with EMA's direction on power rationing results in a breach of their contracted obligations to take or provide electricity or fuel.

sections.label: Singapore's energy challenges
sections.summary: Singapore's energy challenge is to ensure reliable medium- to longer-term supply, meet its 2050 net zero ambition, and do so affordably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: For Singapore, in a setting of a volatile world, our constant energy challenge is to, firstly, ensure reliable energy supply in the medium to longer term; secondly, meet Singapore's 2050 net zero ambition; and thirdly, achieving this at an affordable price.

sections.label: Asian spot gas price volatility
sections.summary: Asian spot gas prices rose from about US$2 per MMBtu in June 2020 to over US$54 in August 2022, remaining around US$14.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Just to illustrate the volatility, the Asian spot gas price moved from a low of about US$2 per metric million British thermal unit (MMBtu) in June 2020, to a high of more than US$54 per MMBtu in around August 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It remains at an elevated level of around US$14 per MMBtu, which is still about seven times from the low in June 2020.

sections.label: Gas unit price and EMA costs
sections.summary: The Bill lets EMA recover costs of energy security, infrastructure development and decarbonisation, making gas unit price determination more complex and less transparent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: With the new framework and the new approach where we need to safeguard securities, the determination of the unit price of gas will become more complex and less transparent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This Bill allows EMA to recover costs of energy security, infrastructure development and decarbonisation-related efforts.

sections.label: Future Energy Fund mandate questions
sections.summary: The $5 billion allocation gives financial space for early moves, and the Minister is asked about the fund's mandate, terms, investment criteria, approval process, governance and nuclear energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The initial $5 billion allocation of funding will give us the financial space to make some early decisive moves and be prepared for a more challenging, volatile and uncertain energy future landscape ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my support, can I ask the Minister to spell out the mandate, the terms and the investment criteria of this fund as well as its approval process and its governance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: My final question to the Minister would be does the investment mandate of the FEF also cover investments in nuclear energy, should it become feasible?

sections.label: Fund launch and renewable energy goal
sections.summary: The fund will be established at the end of this year with $5 billion, first investments next year, and a 10-year time frame for renewable energy to reach 30% of the energy mix.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The fund will be established at the end of this year, with an initial injection of $5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After taking into account due diligence time frames, the first investments through the fund should be made next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This gives a 10-year time frame to achieve our 2035 goal for renewable energy to contribute 30% of our energy mix.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thirty percent is a significant ramp-up and will be predominantly driven by our target to add six gigawatts of low carbon imports, given that the current proportion stands at approximately 1.3%.

sections.label: Electricity consumption and industrial demand
sections.summary: Electricity consumption rose 2.6% between 2021 and 2022 and nearly 25% over 2012 to 2022, with the industrial sector contributing 55% of total energy demand.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Electricity consumption increased by 2.6% between 2021 and 2022, part of a long-term trend of consumption, having increased by nearly 25% over a 10-year period between 2012 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our industrial sector currently contributes 55% of total energy demand.

sections.label: Hydrogen-compatible natural gas power plants
sections.summary: EMA rules require all new and repowered natural gas power plants to be at least 30% hydrogen-compatible from this year, and upcoming plants are hydrogen-compatible.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, EMA introduced rules requiring all new and repowered natural gas power plants to be at least 30% hydrogen-compatible from this year and the few power plants coming up in the next few years are hydrogen-compatible.

sections.label: Mandatory solar panels on buildings
sections.summary: Calls made since 2016 for Singapore to work towards mandatory solar panels on commercial and residential buildings, except in special cases, are repeated.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For this, we would like to repeat our calls made since 2016 for Singapore to work towards solar panels being mandatory on commercial and residential buildings except in special cases.

sections.label: Natural gas electricity generation share
sections.summary: As at end-2022, around 95% of Singapore's electricity is generated using natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As at end-2022, around 95% of Singapore’s electricity is generated using natural gas.

sections.label: Future Energy Fund and EMA powers
sections.summary: The FEF will have an initial $5 billion injection, and the Bill gives EMA power to recover costs of new initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As announced by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong then, the FEF will have an initial injection of $5 billion and invest in critical infrastructure and enhance our security in clean energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, would the $50 million Low-Carbon Energy Research Funding initiative, as announced by Minister Tan See Leng in this House in January 2021, now be parked under the FEF?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Or the National Environment Agency’s Energy Efficiency Grant, which offers grants for manufacturing companies to adopt energy-efficient technologies, would that now be dealt under the FEF instead?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This Bill is also going to give EMA the power to recover the costs of providing new initiatives to strengthen energy security, develop a competitive market, and/or support the decarbonisation of the power sector.

sections.label: EMA direction power usage count
sections.summary: It asks how many times EMA has directed electricity market participants to act against their commercial decision-making.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: To date, how many times has EMA exercised the power to direct electricity market participants to take any action that would otherwise be in their own commercial decision-making domain?

sections.label: Solar and electricity import targets
sections.summary: It asks what percentage of electricity solar will supply by 2030 and how much of the 30% import target is attained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Assuming we achieve our solar deployment target of at least two gigawatt-peak (GWp) by 2030, what percentage of our electricity needs will solar energy be able to supply?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Against our expectation of importing around 30% of our electricity from foreign countries by 2035, how many percent have we attained as of today?

sections.label: Future electricity source mix
sections.summary: It asks how the mix of electricity sources is envisaged to change over time to hit 2030 and 2050 emissions targets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In order to hit our emissions targets by 2030 and 2050, how do we envisage the mix of electricity sources to change over time?

sections.label: Wholesale power price increase
sections.summary: In 2021, wholesale power prices averaged $115 per megawatt-hour from January to September, then soared to $635 by October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2021, wholesale power prices averaged $115 per megawatt-hour from January to September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, by October, these prices soared to $635 per megawatt-hour, a fivefold increase.

sections.label: FEF creation and investment
sections.summary: The FEF is created with an initial investment of $5 billion as a vital step.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The creation of the FEF, with an initial investment of $5 billion, is a vital step in this direction.

sections.label: Solar energy and battery storage
sections.summary: Studies show about 300 MWhr of battery storage is needed per two GWp of solar; Singapore has 1.5 GWp solar and a 285-MWhr system in Jurong Island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Studies have shown that for every two GWp of solar energy, around 300-megawatt hour (MWhr) of Battery Energy Storage Systems is needed to mitigate these short-term disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, Singapore has 1.5 GWp of solar capacity and a centralised 285-MWhr Battery Energy Storage System in Jurong Island.

sections.label: Access to critical energy infrastructure
sections.summary: The Bill directs owners of critical energy assets to allow licensees access with reasonable compensation, and asks whether Battery Energy Storage Systems are included.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, the facilitation of access to critical infrastructure involves directing owners of critical energy assets to allow licensees access, with reasonable compensation for the owner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that EMA has provided a list of critical energy infrastructure, but I would like to ask whether Battery Energy Storage Systems will be included.

sections.label: Solar deployment target and regulatory bottlenecks
sections.summary: Singapore is more than halfway to its 2,000 megawatt-peak solar target by 2030, but must minimise regulatory bottlenecks for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, we are already more than halfway to achieving our solar power deployment target of 2,000 megawatt-peak by 2030, but we must minimise regulatory bottlenecks to facilitate businesses in rolling out their solar initiatives more swiftly.

sections.label: Timely establishment of CGE
sections.summary: Businesses look forward to the establishment of the CGE and it is essential it is implemented in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Businesses are looking forward to the establishment of the CGE and it is essential that it is implemented in a timely manner.

sections.label: FEF establishment under EMA
sections.summary: The Bill proposes establishing the FEF under EMA with an initial $5 billion to support low-carbon energy adoption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes the establishment of the FEF under EMA with an initial amount of $5 billion to support Singapore's adoption of low-carbon energy sources.

sections.label: Natural gas and Gasco
sections.summary: About 95% of Singapore's electricity comes from natural gas, and the Bill proposes a CGE, or Gasco, to centralise gas procurement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: About 95% of Singapore's electricity is generated by natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes setting up the CGE, or referred to as "Gasco", to centralise gas procurement.

sections.label: EMA cost recovery amendments
sections.summary: The Bill proposes amendments letting EMA recover costs for initiatives and services that strengthen energy security, develop a competitive market or decarbonise the power sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes amendments to allow EMA to recover costs for introduction of initiatives and services that strengthen energy security, develop a competitive market or decarbonise the power sector.

sections.label: FEF infrastructure investments
sections.summary: The FEF supports infrastructure investments for Singapore's carbon-neutral transition, backing high-cost, high-risk projects, securing low-carbon energy supplies and keeping Singapore an attractive investment destination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The FEF supports infrastructure investments for Singapore's carbon-neutral transition, backing projects with high costs and risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It secures low-carbon energy supplies, advancing decarbonisation goals and ensures Singapore remains an attractive investment destination.

sections.label: Questions on business aid and FEF
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether there will be Government assistance or incentives for businesses to adapt, and what projects the FEF can invest in and how funds will be prioritised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Minister can address if there will be any Government assistance or incentives to help these businesses adapt?

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, what are the specific types of projects or initiatives that the FEF can invest in and how will the allocation of funds be prioritised among different projects?

sections.label: Rising electricity prices and sufficiency
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore's electricity prices will only go up, and that despite energy deals and partnerships, energy sufficiency will be hard without drastic lifestyle and economic changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, electricity prices for Singapore will only go up and that is the harsh reality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, despite our Government’s best efforts to forge energy deals and partnerships with diverse countries and this is a really important effort, we will still be hard pressed to reach energy sufficiency without making drastic changes to our lifestyle and the way we organise our economic activity.

sections.label: EMA power rationing and public education
sections.summary: The speaker supports EMA's power rationing powers for emergencies, suggesting public education and small-scale rationing exercises, citing Mr Neil Parekh's idea of rationing drills like fire drills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Although this Bill focuses on ensuring energy security in supply, its proposal to empower EMA to implement power rationing during emergencies could be helpful for public education towards becoming a reduced-demand nation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand the anxiety that people naturally would feel about such a prospect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, the way to reduce this anxiety is not to avoid the issue altogether, but to build up our people's confidence that things will be okay and can be okay even if we find ourselves having to have one day, a nationwide power rationing exercise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I like Mr Neil Parekh's suggestions of electricity rationing drills like fire drills and I suggest that the Government undertake intentional public education and begin small-scale electricity rationing exercises for short windows of time in limited geographical areas to make it a part of every Singaporean’s awareness that electricity shortage could be a very real possibility in the coming decades, given the current climate, technological and geopolitical realities.

sections.label: Water and energy security challenges
sections.summary: Singapore achieved water self-sufficiency in the mid-2010s after four decades and 1961 and 1963 crises, and attaining energy security is urgent and monumental.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the past, Singapore had to deal with water supply being an existential threat, so this is not new to us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We only managed to achieve water self-sufficiency in the mid-2010s, with more than four decades of efforts, after having had water crises in 1961 and 1963 that necessitated water rationing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Attaining energy security in a highly urban and modernised state like Singapore is an urgent and monumental task, made even more challenging by the reliance on the numerous creature comforts like air-conditioning and constant wifi that many Singaporeans are used to and now take for granted.

sections.label: Nationwide Unplug Day idea
sections.summary: The passage asks readers to imagine the benefits of a nationwide Unplug Day for a collective digital detox from gadgets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Imagine the benefits of a nationwide "Unplug Day", where we take a collective digital detox from our gadgets.

sections.label: Energy sufficiency shared responsibility
sections.summary: The passage states that the path towards energy sufficiency does not and should not rest only on the Ministries involved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The path towards energy sufficiency does not and should not be on the shoulders of only the Ministries involved.

sections.label: Bill guardrails for electricity market
sections.summary: The Bill introduces electricity market guardrails by regulating centralised gas procurement and letting EMA recover costs for energy security, competition and decarbonisation initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One of the objectives of the Bill is to introduce guardrails for our electricity market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is by: establishing regulations for centralised gas procurement and allowing EMA to recover costs for initiatives to boost our energy security, develop a competitive market and support the power sector’s decarbonisation.

sections.label: Sliding scale and EMA powers
sections.summary: The passage suggests a sliding scale for cost burdens and lists Bill powers for EMA over infrastructure access, repurposing approval and emergency power rationing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I suggest that the Ministry consider introducing a sliding scale based on the size and financial capability of the entities involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This approach would protect small and medium enterprises and lower-income consumers from disproportionate cost burdens, ensuring that the cost of decarbonisation is shared equitably. : To strengthen EMA’s regulation of the power sector, the Bill will empower EMA to: direct owners of critical energy infrastructure to allow access by licensees when necessary in the public interest; require owners of key energy assets to obtain approval before repurposing these infrastructure for other uses; and implement power rationing during emergencies.

sections.label: Clarification on emergency power rationing
sections.summary: The passage seeks clarification from the Minister on the criteria defining an emergency that justifies power rationing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As for the provision for power rationing during emergencies, I seek clarification from the Minister on the criteria to be used to define an emergency that justifies power rationing.

sections.label: FEF creation and $5 billion injection
sections.summary: The FEF, introduced in Budget 2024, received an initial $5 billion injection to support the low-carbon energy transition and sustainable energy infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My first point is on the creation of the FEF and the initial injection of $5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The FEF introduced during Budget 2024 is intended to support our transition towards low-carbon energy sources and provide important funding for a more sustainable energy infrastructure.

sections.label: McKinsey net-zero spending estimate
sections.summary: A 2022 McKinsey Global Institute estimate suggested $9.2 trillion in annual average spending on physical assets is needed to reach net-zero emissions by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One estimate by the McKinsey Global Institute in 2022 suggested that $9.2 trillion in annual average spending on physical assets alone will be required to transform the global economy to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050.

sections.label: Gas procurement coverage percentage question
sections.summary: The question asks what percentage of gas procurement the centralised procurement regime will cover after excluding non-power sector consumers and legacy gas contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can Minister share what percentage of gas procurement will be covered under the centralised procurement regime after excluding non-power sector consumers and legacy gas contracts?

sections.label: Cost recovery mechanism and gas reliance
sections.summary: The passage asks how the cost recovery mechanism will be implemented, how EMA will estimate costs, and how mis-estimations will be corrected, noting 95% reliance on imported natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how the cost recovery mechanism will be implemented?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How will EMA derive its "reasonable estimation" of the costs that will be incurred?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the event that the estimation is inaccurate, what are the mechanisms to correct the mis-estimation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our reliance on imported natural gas – 95% of our energy mix – makes us vulnerable to global market shifts.

sections.label: Hydrogen power plants and power needs
sections.summary: Singapore is reported to have at least nine hydrogen-compatible power plants by 2030, with hydrogen expected to meet 50% of power needs by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On low-carbon hydrogen, it was reported that Singapore will have at least nine hydrogen-compatible power plants by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hydrogen is expected to meet 50% of our power needs by 2050.

sections.label: Green hydrogen cost versus natural gas
sections.summary: Green hydrogen currently costs three to five times more than natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Green hydrogen currently costs three to five times more than natural gas.

sections.label: FEF transparency and market distortions
sections.summary: The Minister should clarify how potential market distortions will be addressed, and greater transparency is needed in managing the FEF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Minister should clarify how potential market distortions will be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Greater transparency is needed in managing the FEF.

sections.label: Energy story and imported gas
sections.summary: The Bill is an opportunity to rewrite the energy story, balancing innovation with caution, protecting the vulnerable and committing to sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We are heavily reliant on imported natural gas, just as we once were with water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill represents our opportunity to rewrite the energy story as we did with water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If we get it right, if we balance innovation with caution, protect our most vulnerable and remain steadfast in our commitment to sustainability, we can transform our energy landscape.

sections.label: U-Save and Climate Friendly vouchers
sections.summary: Eligible households receive 2.5 times regular U-Save, up to $950, and all HDB households are eligible for $300 in Climate Friendly Households vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For example, eligible households will receive 2.5 times the amount of regular U-Save, or up to $950, in this financial year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: More than 950,000 Singaporean Housing and Development Board (HDB) households are expected to benefit from this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: All HDB households are also eligible for $300 in vouchers through the Climate Friendly Households Programme to lower the upfront cost of purchasing energy-efficient appliances and in turn, allow households to achieve savings on utility bills in the long run.

sections.label: Advanced electricity meters rollout
sections.summary: Advanced electricity meters will be rolled out to all HDB households by 2026.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Advanced electricity meters will be rolled out to all HDB households by 2026.

sections.label: Cost of energy transition
sections.summary: The energy transition will be costly and is expected to cost far more than the $5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The energy transition will be costly and is expected to cost far more than the $5 billion.

sections.label: FEF purpose for low-carbon future
sections.summary: The FEF is not meant to fund such costs but to catalyse and seed support in strategic infrastructural investments for a low-carbon future.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The FEF is not meant to fund such costs, but rather, it is meant to catalyse and seed support in strategic infrastructural investments for a low-carbon future.

sections.label: Undersea cables and hydrogen projects
sections.summary: Potential projects include undersea cables to import low-carbon electricity and hydrogen terminals and pipelines if hydrogen use is adopted and scaled up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Potential projects include undersea cables to import low-carbon electricity as well as hydrogen terminals and pipelines, if we decide to adopt and scale up the use of hydrogen.

sections.label: Ring-fencing funds for power decarbonisation
sections.summary: Funds will be ring-fenced for infrastructure development needed to decarbonise the power sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: First, we will ring-fence the use of funds to infrastructure development needed to decarbonise the power sector.

sections.label: Shared access directives and appeals
sections.summary: If access is critical and no agreement is reached, EMA will issue a directive, then an Appeal Panel will determine terms case-by-case.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If access is deemed critical to system needs and no agreement is reached, EMA will issue a directive for the shared access and give both parties a 30-day period to agree.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If agreement is still not reached, an Appeal Panel will independently determine the terms on a case-by-case basis, considering industry practices, prevailing market conditions, the nature of the infrastructure and case-specific circumstances.

sections.label: Gas contracting level for gencos
sections.summary: About 75% of Singapore's gas consumption is by the power sector, and EMA will impose a standardised minimum gas contracting level.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To Mr Louis Ng’s question, around 75% of Singapore’s gas consumption is by the power sector and will be procured by the Gasco in the steady state.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: While gencos are well-contracted for the immediate future, EMA will impose a standardised minimum gas contracting level under this framework, to ensure they continue to contract sufficient fuel from the Gasco.

sections.label: Gencos lack economies of scale
sections.summary: Singapore's power sector needs six to seven million tonnes of natural gas annually, but six main gencos each contract only about one million tonne.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Singapore’s power sector currently needs around six to seven million tonnes of natural gas annually, but with six main gencos each contracting, on the average, for only one million tonne, they do not have economies of scale.

sections.label: Gasco as Government-owned company
sections.summary: The Gasco is expected to be set up as a fully Government-owned company by the end of this financial year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Louis Ng and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how gas prices for gencos will be determined.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We expect to set up the Gasco as a fully Government-owned company by the end of this financial year.

sections.label: Gasco gas pricing
sections.summary: The Gasco will price gas on a cost-plus basis, charging gencos for gas purchased plus a regulated fee covering operating costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Gasco will price gas on a cost-plus basis, with gencos charged for the gas they purchase, plus a regulated fee to cover the Gasco’s operating costs.

sections.label: Emergency definition in Bill
sections.summary: The Bill defines an emergency as an electricity shortage, a likely shortage, or a threat to secure power transmission system operation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: An emergency is defined in the Bill as a situation where, an electricity shortage has occurred or where EMA assesses that a shortage is likely or if no measures are taken, the secure operation of our power transmission system will be threatened.

sections.label: Power rationing prioritisation framework
sections.summary: MTI and EMA intend to establish a prioritisation framework with guidelines for load reductions, prioritising critical services and residents' daily power needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: MTI and EMA intend to establish a prioritisation framework, outlining clear guidelines for EMA’s intended order of load reductions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have started preliminary consultations with some stakeholders on this and further consultations will follow.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The intent of the prioritisation framework is to minimise the impact of power rationing on society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, we will give priority to services that are critical to Singapore’s security, economic and social needs, such as medical and telecommunications services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will also give priority for residents to have access to power for daily needs.
